metadata.title: MIM-Flow Forward Data and Model
metadata.description:
This record provides the trained spectrum-prediction models and the associated high-precision quantum-chemical dataset developed for MIM-Flow. The dataset contains vibronically resolved emission spectra of MR-TADF molecules generated in this work.

The spectra were calculated using the ESD module in ORCA 6.0 within the Franck–Condon approximation. Ground- and first-excited-state equilibrium geometries were obtained at the B3LYP-D3BJ/def2-SVP and TDA-B3LYP-D3BJ/def2-SVP levels, respectively. The corresponding vibrational information and adiabatic \(S_1-S_0\) energy differences were used to construct the vibronic emission spectra. Vibrational modes below 50 cm\(^{-1}\) were excluded, with the remaining computational settings described in the https://chemrxiv.org/doi/abs/10.26434/chemrxiv.15005860/v1. Generating such a high-precision vibronically resolved emission spectrum typically requires approximately 500-700 CPU core-hours per molecule, as the computational cost varies with molecular size and convergence behavior. 

This record also contains the trained model checkpoints used for spectrum prediction and reward evaluation in MIM-Flow. The models and high-precision quantum-chemical data are released to support reproduction of the reported results and further development of data-driven methods for vibronically resolved excited-state spectra and functional molecular design.
